title: What Makes a Structure Hold?
subtitle: The same region dissolves or persists depending on its surroundings. Refinement can remove its only exit. The receipts show why.
seo_title: Persistence from Geometry: What Makes a Structure Hold?
seo_description: Persistence from Geometry shows how context protects a region and refinement can remove its only exit, with GPU receipts and bound-incidence computations.
author: Devon A. Generally
paper_title: Persistence from Geometry: Context, Refinement and Deterministic Change
social_preview_description: Same hole. Same location. Different surroundings. One dissolves; one holds. Paper Two shows how geometry makes persistence contextual.

figures.placement: After the paragraph beginning The exterior protects the hole
figures.alt_text: Same hole and containing face: the nested field discharges 30 walls and opens 10; the contrast discharges 20 and opens none.
figures.caption: Same hole, different surroundings. Both rows are GPU receipts. The complete nested-field no-exit result is a separate computation over the bound incidence.

figures.placement: End of Refinement can remove an exit
figures.alt_text: Refinement comparison: a single-site field changes from one strict exit to none in a read-only correspondence; the nested field's 64 walls and 30 discharged, 20 opened prediction match its GPU receipt.
figures.caption: Two refinement results, two scopes: the single-site comparison is read-only; the nested prediction is checked by GPU execution on one transported field.

figures.placement: After the first paragraph of Placement matters, and context reaches further
figures.alt_text: Of 480 adjacent pairs, 60 have a strict exit and 420 have none under the recorded offered family. The full classification is computed over bound incidence; GPU receipts witness all 60 exits.
figures.caption: Complete classification over bound incidence; targeted GPU receipts for every predicted exit. The 420 retained pairs are not presented as an exhaustive GPU census.
